Here's a description of the provided plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. A blue line, marked with circular data points and error bars, represents “Final Accuracy.” This line begins at approximately 0.94 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and remains relatively stable, fluctuating between approximately 0.91 and 0.96, before ending at approximately 0.97 at an initial confidence of 0.99. An orange line, marked with triangular data points and error bars, represents “Δ Accuracy.” This line starts at approximately 0.41 at an initial confidence of 0.81, decreases to a minimum of approximately 0.14 at an initial confidence of 0.87, and then increases to approximately 0.18 at an initial confidence of 0.99. A green line, marked with square data points and error bars, represents “Initial Accuracy.” This line begins at approximately 0.59 at an initial confidence of 0.81, increases to a peak of approximately 0.74 at an initial confidence of 0.86, and then decreases to approximately 0.84 at an initial confidence of 0.99.
